# Results — Study 708 (Eurovision-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **a
country's stock market gets a "feel-good" bump when it wins (or hosts) the Eurovision
Song Contest** — the folklore cousin of the Edmans-García-Norli sports-sentiment
effect, aimed at Europe's silliest, most beloved television night instead of the World
Cup. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint
`acb2b3bfb578` (14 country ETFs + the VGK Europe benchmark, one combined panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 14 single-country ETFs + `VGK` (Vanguard FTSE Europe), one combined panel: 7,620 rows, 1996-03-18 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 26 Grand Finals 2000→2025 (2020 COVID-cancelled → 25 contested editions), winner + host country per year (Wikipedia "List of Eurovision Song Contest winners" / "…host cities") |
| Events resolvable | of **50** possible role-events (25 editions × {winner, host}), **25** have both a mapped country ETF *and* VGK coverage around the final: **12 winner**, **13 host** |
| Excluded, by reason | 10× ETF/VGK inception postdates the final · 5× Ukraine (no US-listed ETF ever) · 2× each Estonia, Latvia, Serbia, Russia (ERUS delisted, sanctions), Azerbaijan (no ETF) · 2× 2020 cancelled (COVID-19) |
| Countries in the winner sample | Austria, Denmark, Germany, Israel, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal, Sweden (×3), Switzerland — 9 distinct countries over 12 events |
| Countries in the host sample | + Norway, United Kingdom (host in 2023 "on behalf of" Ukraine) — 11 distinct countries over 13 events |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; Welch *t* for the winner-vs-host third axis |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the Grand Final airs Saturday night (non-trading); **day(-1)** = last close before the final (does not know the winner), **day(0)** = first close after (fully public, ~36-60h old, zero look-ahead). Signal = day(-1)→day(-1)+k; Tradability = day(0)→day(0)+k, net of 2× one-way cost × NAV |
| Data quirks (named) | 2021 hosted by the Netherlands again (rolled over from cancelled 2020); 2023 hosted by the United Kingdom for war-affected Ukraine — the market tested is the UK's, the actual venue |

**Selection, named on the Signal axis:** the sample that survives is systematically the
richer, more-developed half of Europe — five countries (Estonia, Latvia, Serbia,
Azerbaijan, and three-time winner Ukraine) never had a tradable single-country ETF at
all, and Russia's ERUS was effectively erased from the data record after the 2022
sanctions (a vehicle-risk story, like SVXY's twin XIV in study 637). A test that can
only ever answer for the EU-core subset of winners is not testing the full folklore.

## The signal — abnormal return, day(-1) → day(-1)+k (country ETF − VGK)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| winner, 1 week (k=5) | 12 | −0.023% | −0.06 | 8/12 = 66.7% [39.1%, 86.2%] |
| **winner, 1 month (k=21)** | 12 | **+1.634%** | **+2.07** | 10/12 = 83.3% [55.2%, 95.3%] |
| host, 1 week | 13 | −0.220% | −1.01 | 6/13 = 46.2% [23.2%, 70.9%] |
| host, 1 month | 13 | −0.208% | −0.40 | 6/13 = 46.2% [23.2%, 70.9%] |
| combined, 1 week | 25 | −0.125% | −0.56 | 14/25 = 56.0% [37.1%, 73.3%] |
| combined, 1 month | 25 | +0.676% | +1.37 | 16/25 = 64.0% [44.5%, 79.8%] |

Only **one of four** primary cuts nominally clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar — the
**winner, 1-month** cut. It does **not** replicate at the 1-week horizon (*t* = −0.06),
does **not** appear for hosting at either horizon, and the pooled "any Eurovision
achievement" test (the more defensible primary read, since the folklore names both
winning *and* hosting) is **not significant** (*t* = +1.37).

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event, right-tail unless noted)

| cut | observed mean | placebo mean (sd) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **winner, 1 month** | **+1.634%** | +0.087% (0.859%) | **0.038** |
| winner, 1 week | −0.023% | +0.017% (0.467%) | 0.535 |
| host, 1 month | −0.208% | +0.063% (0.804%) | 0.632 |
| host, 1 week | −0.220% | +0.006% (0.413%) | 0.711 |
| combined, 1 month | +0.676% | +0.065% (0.591%) | 0.149 |
| combined, 1 week | −0.125% | +0.013% (0.308%) | 0.675 |

The winner/1-month cut clears both bars (raw *t* = 2.07, placebo *p* = 0.038) — but it
is the *only* one of six cuts that does, exactly the base rate a lucky cut can produce
by chance among several tries.

## Robustness — jackknife on the one cut that clears the bar

Leave-one-out on the 12 winner/1-month events: full-sample *t* = **+2.066**; the
jackknife range is **[+1.711, +2.178]**, and **5 of 12** leave-one-out draws (dropping
Denmark 2013, Sweden 2015, Portugal 2017, Switzerland 2024, or Austria 2025 in turn)
push the estimate **below** the *t* = 2 certification bar. A signal that flips
certified/uncertified depending on which single one of 12 tiny-n events you drop is not
robust.

## Event anatomy — does the shape match "feel-good bump"?

Mean cumulative abnormal return by trading day from day(-1) (the pre-final anchor):

| day | 0 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 21 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| winner | 0.000% | −0.023% | +0.673% | +1.308% | +1.634% |
| host | 0.000% | −0.220% | −0.191% | −0.102% | −0.208% |

If national pride produced a quick feel-good pop, the winner path should jump near day
0-5 and then hold, the way the FOMC vol crush (study 637) resolves in a single session.
Instead the winner path is **flat-to-negative for the first week** and only accumulates
its gain gradually over the following two weeks — a shape that looks more like generic
country-specific drift over a month than an announcement effect tied to a Saturday
night broadcast.

## Tradability — capture, day(0) → day(0)+k, net of costs

Entered at day(0)'s close (the first price *after* the result is public — zero
look-ahead, since the final airs on a non-trading Saturday).

| cut | gross | net @ 5 bps (*t*) | net @ 10 bps (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| winner, 1 week | −0.198% (*t* = −0.56) | −0.298% (−0.84) | −0.398% (−1.12) |
| winner, 1 month | +1.447% (*t* = +1.92) | +1.347% (+1.78) | +1.247% (+1.65) |
| host, 1 week | −0.367% (*t* = −1.88) | −0.467% (**−2.39**) | −0.567% (−2.90) |
| host, 1 month | −0.358% (*t* = −0.71) | −0.458% (−0.91) | −0.558% (−1.11) |
| combined, 1 week | −0.286% (*t* = −1.47) | −0.386% (−1.99) | −0.486% (−2.50) |
| combined, 1 month | +0.509% (*t* = +1.07) | +0.409% (+0.86) | +0.309% (+0.65) |

Two placebo checks on the two cuts that *look* interesting:

- **Winner, 1 month, net @ 5 bps**: observed +1.347% vs placebo mean −0.014% (sd
  0.857%) → **p = 0.058** — misses the bar entirely once you charge costs and require
  a zero-look-ahead entry.
- **Host, 1 week, net @ 5 bps** *looked* significant on the naive one-sample *t*
  (**−2.39**) — hosting seems to produce a sell-the-news dip. But the random-window
  placebo says this magnitude of weekly tracking difference against VGK is **common**
  for these tickers: observed −0.467% vs placebo mean −0.100% (sd 0.418%) →
  **p = 0.180**. The naive *t* oversold it; there is no certified host-week effect,
  positive or negative.

No cut clears **t ≥ 2 net of costs with placebo confirmation**. Tradability = Mirage.

## Third axis — winning vs hosting: does it matter which one you did?

Welch *t* of winner's abnormal return minus host's, same event set:

| horizon | winner mean | host mean | Welch *t* (winner − host) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| signal, 1 week | −0.023% | −0.220% | +0.43 |
| **signal, 1 month** | **+1.634%** | −0.208% | **+1.95** |
| capture, 1 week (net) | −0.298% | −0.467% | +0.42 |
| **capture, 1 month (net)** | **+1.347%** | −0.458% | **+1.99** |

At the 1-month horizon, winning consistently beats hosting by a Welch *t* of
**~1.95-1.99** — a hair below the certification bar both times. Directionally
consistent, statistically just short.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (asset, benchmark) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.75, like a country ETF
vs a regional benchmark) with a scheduled synthetic event calendar and a TUNABLE
planted "national-pride bump"; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.09** (sd 1.14), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted bump = +1.0% (seed 708) | **+2.98** |
| planted bump = +2.0% (seed 708) | **+4.49** |

The detector recovers a planted bump and mostly does not fire on the null (2/20 seeds
at |t| ≥ 2, in line with the ~5-10% false-positive rate expected at this modest n — not
a bias in the detector). *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** One of four primary cuts (winner, 1-month) nominally clears
  *t* ≥ 2 with a placebo *p* = 0.038 — but it does not replicate at the 1-week horizon,
  does not appear for hosting, fails when winner and host are pooled (the more
  defensible primary read, *t* = +1.37), loses certification in 5 of 12 leave-one-out
  draws, and its shape (flat for a week, then a slow 2-week drift) does not match the
  claimed quick-pop mechanism. Literature offers no real anchor for this specific claim
  (unlike study 235's Edmans backing) — a marginal tape whisper, not a real signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No cut clears *t* ≥ 2 net of costs with placebo
  confirmation. The best case (winner, 1-month, net) is *t* = +1.78, placebo
  *p* = 0.058; the naive-looking host/1-week "sell-the-news" effect (*t* = −2.39)
  evaporates under its own placebo (*p* = 0.180).
- **"Winning beats hosting?" — MIXED.** Winner point estimates beat host's at both
  horizons and both measurements, and the 1-month Welch *t* (winner − host) sits at
  +1.95 to +1.99 — a consistent direction, one hair short of certified.
